_comment: Tool policy for the visual critic: the fresh `claude -p` session that
grades a contact sheet against the rubric and against the reigning
champion. It is the narrowest profile the harness ships, for two reasons.
First, the critic's prompt is UNTRUSTED TEXT. The rubric comes from the
target repo (.creative/rubric.md) or from a planner-written brief, and the
frames it looks at were produced by the very worker it is grading. A critic
with a shell is a critic a bad rubric can turn into a shell. There is no
Bash rule here at all, and Bash is denied besides: permission patterns
match the head of a command line and cannot see what it goes on to run.
Second, a critic that can write is a critic that can grade its own work.
No Edit, no Write, no Task — the whole point of this stage is a cold read
by something that had no hand in the render. Read and Glob are what it
needs and all it gets: the reference board, the champion sheet, the
challenger sheet, and the JSON it returns through --json-schema.
The network tools are denied so the images and the rubric cannot leave the
machine, and the harness's own secrets are denied by path for the same
